title: Failure vector map and fault-origins explorer
creator: Marco Nguyen
description:
Goal: Build a failure-vector mapping and an interactive explorer that surfaces the origin and prevalence of inference failures across traces, metrics, and logs. The explorer will let engineers pivot on request attributes (model_version, route, sequence_length, payload_size, batch_size, region, hardware_tier) and see a ranked set of failure modes (timeouts, overload/backpressure, model runtime errors, HTTP/gRPC status distributions, OOMs, KV-cache misses). This ticket covers the schema, trace hook placement, pipeline enrichment, dashboard UI wireframe, SLI definitions, and an initial rollout plan.

Why: Current dashboards give aggregate error rates and raw traces but do not tie request vectors to failure modes. That makes root-cause work slow and leads to noisy SLO alerts. A vector-based view will speed triage and enable targeted remediation (retry/backoff rules, routing changes, model fallbacks, autoscaling triggers).

Scope and deliverables:
- Telemetry schema: new structured fields (failure_vector, failure_reason, request_features) for logs/metrics/traces.
- Trace hooks: annotate spans at pre-routing, serving-runtime-enter, kernel-dispatch, model-exec-complete, kv-cache-lookup with the new attributes.
- Metric & log pipeline changes: enrich spans with model metadata and push compact failure counters to metrics pipeline (rules below).
- Explorer dashboard: heatmap of vector -> failure mode frequency, sortable by impact (p95 latency, error budget burn), with trace-link deep dive and suggested remediation actions.
- SLO mapping: map existing SLOs to vectors (e.g., route X + seq_len>2048) and create per-vector alerting for high-burn.
- Performance budget: instrumentation overhead must be <5% p99 increase in per-request latency in canary.

Implementation approach: We will add a lightweight failure_vector tag (string) that concatenates normalized attributes (route|model:variant|seq_bucket|payload_bucket) and a failure_reason tag from an enumerated taxonomy (timeout, overload_backpressure, model_runtime_error, http_4xx, http_5xx, grpc_cancelled, grpc_unavailable, oom, invalid_input, kv_cache_miss). Metrics pipeline will emit failure_vector.count and failure_vector.latency_p95. Traces where failure_reason != "none" will be sampled at higher rate and linked from the dashboard.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Full attribute explosion vs compact vector key: we choose compact vector keys to keep metric cardinality manageable while retaining pivotability in the dashboard.
- Client-side vs server-side instrumentation: server-side to ensure consistency across deployments (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Sampling: uniform vs adaptive. We will implement adaptive sampling that boosts capture for error vectors to avoid losing rare failure contexts.

Monitoring and rollout: start with canary on a single routing pool, validate overhead and signal quality for 72h, then expand to 25% of traffic, then platform-wide. Dashboard and schema will be documented in Confluence and pushed as a spec for Private deployment operators.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry schema published in Confluence and merged to platform repo
Trace hook implementation merged to runtime with feature flag
Metrics pipeline emits failure_vector.count and failure_vector.latency_p95 for canary pool
Explorer dashboard (heatmap + trace-link) available in Console behind feature flag
Adaptive error sampling active and verified for at least 72h
Instrumentation overhead measured and <=5% p99 latency for canary
notes: Decision: use compact vector key to limit cardinality (format: route|model@variant|seq_bucket|payload_bucket)
Decision: failure_reason taxonomy will be the canonical set for all observability layers; any new reasons must be added via PR and a migration note
Follow-up: create runbook mapping top 10 vectors to remediation playbooks (retry policy, route weight change, model fallback)
Privacy: avoid logging raw user prompt; only metadata buckets retained per data retention policy
